scene_summary: A small office with a blind-covered window, low cubby shelf, two swivel chairs, tables, a floor lamp, and a potted plant.
overall_evidence: The reconstruction captures many recognizable furnishings and their broad arrangement, but the viewpoint exposes a much wider, open room, the prominent paneled door is not visibly reproduced, and the floor and furniture surfaces are substantially lighter and less textured than the reference. The chairs and foreground tables also differ in apparent orientation and presentation.

main_defects.description: The reconstruction is viewed from a higher, more distant and wider vantage, exposing the tops and outer edges of walls and much more empty floor instead of the enclosed close interior view.
main_defects.evidence: In the reference the walls fill the background and the foreground furniture is cropped; in the reconstruction the wall tops, exterior gray background, and extensive floor are visible.
main_defects.uncertainty: Some apparent differences in spacing and scale may be consequences of the changed viewpoint rather than actual placement errors.

main_defects.description: The large dark paneled door is not visibly represented as a door in the reconstruction.
main_defects.evidence: The reference has a prominent dark eight-panel door on the right wall; the reconstruction shows only a thin dark sliver near the right wall, without a comparable visible door face.
main_defects.uncertainty: A door could be present but nearly edge-on or occluded by the wall from this viewpoint.

main_defects.description: The reconstructed floor and furniture are much paler and flatter in appearance, losing the reference's brown wood grain floor and dark gray tabletop surfaces.
main_defects.evidence: The reference floor has conspicuous varied brown wood texture and the tabletops are charcoal gray; the reconstruction floor is nearly white with simple seams and the tabletops are light gray.
main_defects.uncertainty: Lighting and exposure may account for part, but not necessarily all, of the color difference.

main_defects.description: The chair shells present different directions and silhouettes: the reference has two obliquely oriented, side-visible chairs, while the reconstruction shows the nearer chair almost squarely from behind and the other more directly face-on.
main_defects.evidence: The reference foreground chair's seat projects prominently to the right, whereas the reconstruction foreground chair reads as a centered, symmetric back.
main_defects.uncertainty: The changed camera angle contributes to the apparent orientation difference.

main_defects.description: The window and cubby shelf occupy a much smaller part of the image and appear less dominant within the back wall.
main_defects.evidence: The reference window spans roughly a quarter of the image width, and its shelf is prominent; both appear comparatively small and distant in the reconstruction.
main_defects.uncertainty: This is an image-space proportion difference; the wider camera view may explain much of it without implying incorrect object dimensions.

strengths: The blind-covered rectangular window sits above a light wood cubby shelf.
A slender floor lamp stands to the left of the shelf and a narrow white cabinet stands to its right.
Two wheeled pedestal chairs, foreground tables, and a spiky plant in a teal pot are recognizable and broadly arranged in the same office setting.
uncertainty: This is an initial automated image-based estimate, not a human rating or validated metric. Different framing and occlusion limit judgments about actual 3D dimensions, chair rotation, door presence, and object spacing; hidden geometry is not assessed.
